descriptions.text: Sheol Brick. If Santa gives coal to the regular naughty kids, he'd probably give this stuff to history's greatest villains, like Hans Gruber and the guy who invented those shoes with the individual toes built in. It burns a lot hotter and a lot longer than regular coal. And when I say "a lot longer," I mean until the end of your lifetime. So like a week or more. To save you distress, I'm not going to tell you where this came from. That was a lie! It's a baby corpse!

beats.headline: Running on dead babies
beats.text: Fire Brandy's own description explains her trade. A Lesser Demon in labour gives birth for about sixty days, fifteen to eighteen thousand babies, one roughly every five minutes, and only one in ten thousand is viable. The rest shrivel and harden into a valuable resource called Sheol Bricks, which burn long and hot when exposed to fire. A stoker who learns water magic seals herself in a boiler, keeps a big engine humming almost by itself, and disposes of her failed young in the same stroke. The train is running on dead babies. Holy crap, thinks Carl, that's fucked up.

beats.headline: The box in the cab
beats.text: Fire Brandy points him to a small box at the back of the cab, covered in gore where the driver or the war mage was pushed against it. Carl lifts the lid and pulls out a black chunk. Its description promises not to tell him where it came from, to save him distress, and then admits that was a lie: it's a baby corpse. He drops it in revulsion and wipes his hand on his cloak. There are about fifty bricks in the chest. He takes a deep breath, picks up the entire box and adds it to his inventory. He shudders.

beats.headline: Several hundred, still burning
beats.text: Carl and Donut find Fire Brandy still aboard the idling Nightmare, still giving birth, refusing a pair of dwarven engineers who want to take the train somewhere: there is nowhere to go, she tells them, and they leave when Carl arrives. Her persona has slipped into something more melancholy. He has shown one of the rocks to Mordecai, who was nearly beside himself and told him to get as many as possible, so Carl asks if she can part with any. She lets him take several hundred still-burning pieces, along with a few dozen that have not yet caught fire. She would give him all of it, she says, but she needs to keep the fire hot and her babies happy.
